items.headline: Min Woo Lee lights up East Lake — a bogey-free 62 with $10M on the line
items.body: In his first-ever Tour Championship, Min Woo Lee opened with eight birdies and zero bogeys for a 62 to grab a two-shot lead over Viktor Hovland. Fun detail: he says he tuned up by watching his own highlights on YouTube.
items.say: Did you see Min Woo Lee open the Tour Championship with a 62? Bloke prepped by watching YouTube — apparently it works.

items.headline: Paige Bueckers punches her first ticket — and now the whole WNBA field is set
items.body: The No. 1 pick dropped 22 points and 11 assists as Dallas beat Portland to grab the eighth and final playoff spot — the Wings' first trip back to the postseason since 2023, and a franchise-record win total with games to spare.
items.say: Paige Bueckers just dragged the Wings back to the playoffs in her rookie year — the whole WNBA bracket's locked now.

items.headline: Cold as ice, then a hero — Ha-Seong Kim walks off the Dodgers
items.body: Kim was mired in a brutal slump (a hit in his last 27 at-bats) when he came off the bench in the ninth and laced a walk-off single, sending the Braves past LA 6-5 for their third straight win and the season-series tiebreaker.
items.say: Ha-Seong Kim was ice cold for weeks, then comes off the bench and walks off the Dodgers — you can't script baseball.

items.headline: CS2's back on the big stage — BLAST Open Fall is live, playoffs head to Porto
items.body: After a summer of majors, the world's top Counter-Strike teams are back at it: BLAST Open Fall (Aug 26–Sep 6) has $1.1M on the line, with the group stage in Copenhagen before a live-crowd finale in Portugal. NAVI vs M80 already pulled nearly 300K viewers.
items.say: Counter-Strike's already back — BLAST Open Fall is on, finals in Porto. Have you caught any of it?

items.headline: The title race gets real this weekend — Liverpool, Chelsea and Spurs all in action
items.body: It's the last Premier League weekend before Monday's transfer deadline: Liverpool host Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Tottenham face Newcastle, and Chelsea's Xabi Alonso era rolls on at home to Brighton on Sunday.
items.say: Premier League's back this weekend — Liverpool Saturday, Chelsea Sunday, and deadline day right after. Who are you watching?

items.headline: Alabama Shakes are back — 'I Must Be Dreaming' is their first album in 11 years
items.body: Brittany Howard and co. return with their third album and first since 2015's 'Sound & Color' — now a trio, and picking up right where their soulful, Grammy-winning rock left off.
items.say: Alabama Shakes finally dropped a new album — first one in eleven years. Brittany Howard's voice still gives me chills.

items.headline: Billy Strings gets personal — 'So Much for Goodbyes' is a tribute to his late mom
items.body: The bluegrass phenom's fifth album is his most personal yet — 16 tracks written in the wake of his mother's passing, and it's already one of the biggest roots releases of the year.
items.say: New Billy Strings album's out and it's a tribute to his mom — heard it's a heavy, beautiful one.

items.headline: Interpol return to the shadows — 'This Mirror Weighs a Ton' is out
items.body: The New York post-punk mainstays are back with a new album of the moody, guitar-driven sound that made them 2000s indie royalty. One more heavyweight on a stacked New Music Friday.
items.say: Interpol put out a new record today — that broody NYC sound is right in the pocket for a rainy afternoon.

items.headline: 'The Further' reopens — Insidious 6 brings the horror franchise back to theaters
items.body: 'Insidious: Out of the Further' revives the hit supernatural series with a new family, a new terror, and Lin Shaye back as fan-favorite Elise. It's off to a solid start — a $25M-plus debut for the sixth film.
items.say: The new Insidious is out — perfect if you want a jump-scare night. Are you a horror person or a hide-behind-the-couch person?
